body: Split-adjusted (10:1, Oct 2024): ~$4-7 in 2022-early 2023 -> intraday ~$122.9 (Mar 2024), joining the S&P 500: ~17-30x [prices from memory, unverified]. Revenue roughly doubled FY23->FY24 (~$7bn -> ~$15bn) on Nvidia GPU server racks and liquid cooling. Then: gross margin fell to 11.3% (June 2024 qtr) from 17%; Hindenburg short report (Aug 27 2024: accounting red flags, related parties, export-control issues); 10-K delayed; Ernst & Young resigned Oct 30 2024 saying it could no longer rely on management/audit-committee representations (-33% day). Low ~$17 (Nov 2024), ~-86% from peak [unverified exact]. BDO hired Nov 2024; overdue reports filed Feb 2025 without restatement, but BDO issued adverse opinions on internal controls. Margins kept sliding (9.3% FQ1'26; 6.4% adj FQ2'26). March 2026: US indicted co-founder Wally Liaw and two others for diverting ~$2.5bn of Nvidia-based servers (~$510m reaching China); stock -33% in a day; company not charged. EARLY RED FLAGS visible before the peak: 2018 Nasdaq delisting for late filings, 2020 SEC accounting settlement (~$17.5m) [unverified], rehiring of executives tied to that episode, related-party suppliers, and falling gross margin while revenue soared (a commoditised assembler). Who caught it: momentum buyers on the way up; Hindenburg on the way down. LESSON: revenue hypergrowth in a low-moat assembler plus a known governance history is a peak-hype setup; margin compression is the first tell.

data.early_signals: up: AI rack share; down: prior SEC case, 2018 delisting, GM 17%->11%
data.eps_vs_rerating: EPS + rerating up; margin collapse down
data.lesson: governance history + commodity margins = fragile multibagger

title: Super Micro 2023-2026: AI-server 17x, then -86% on governance
